news.headline: Explainer: why NAC fields now say 'Elite' and 'Challenger'
news.fit: SECONDARY A (parent-service explainer) — directly explains our own results
news.summary: The October NAC was the first under USA Fencing's new structure: Cadet and Division I events with more than 168 entries split into an Elite tier (capped at 112, filled from the Unified Points List as of Sept. 24) and a Challenger tier (all other registrants). At the November NAC the split applies to Cadet, Junior and Division I. A Sept. 28 update said USA Fencing let some fencers opt into Elite for Oct/Nov as a transition measure, apologized for how 2025-26 points carryover was communicated, and expanded the points review group (now incl. small-club voices), meeting after the Oct and Nov NACs.
key_facts: Split cutoff: 15 days before tournament (Oct NAC: Sept 24; Nov NAC: Nov 5)
Elite cap 112; Cadet Elite = top 112 Cadet UPL; Div I Elite = top 72 Senior + 24 Junior + 16 Cadet UPL
Challenger fencers who opt in can move up to Elite as spots open, until 5 p.m. local the night before
Two-year trial; points review group meets after Oct and Nov NACs; feedback channel open
New points system took effect Aug 1, 2026

news.headline: Vet Worlds in Tbilisi: U.S. men's epee veterans grab silver, silver and two team bronzes
news.fit: SECONDARY B (fun 'fencing is for life' angle; parents who fence)
news.summary: At the Veteran World Championships in Tbilisi, Georgia (Oct 9-17), Sean Ameli (USA) lost the Veteran 60 men's epee final 9-8 in overtime to France's Olivier Guilbert in a field of 96, and Bruce Jugan (USA) took silver in Veteran 70 men's epee, losing 10-5 to Belgium's Jean Stock (field of 74) after a back-arm-blocking penalty swung the bout. The U.S. won bronze in both the Veteran 40-59 men's epee team (beat Poland 45-33) and the Grand Veteran men's epee team (beat France 45-40). Women's epee runs Oct 12-14.
key_facts: Tbilisi Vet Worlds: Oct 9-17, 2026; 65 nations, 1,273 athletes (FIE tournament page)
V60 ME: Guilbert (FRA) d. Ameli (USA) 9-8 OT; field 96
V70 ME: Stock (BEL) d. Jugan (USA) 10-5; field 74; Stock repeat champion
V40 ME: Remoue (FRA) gold, field 87 — ex-foilist until 28, used foil-style cutover
V50 ME: Le Treut (FRA) d. Kerminen (FIN) 10-6; field 110
Team bronzes for USA: V40-59 ME team (Gaines, Hallman, Hedges, Hurme, Tsinis); Grand Vet ME team (Ameli, Hudson, Jugan, Moreau, Nixon) — note FIE spells 'Jeffey Hudson', likely typo, verify
Women's epee: V70 & V50 Oct 12; V60 & V40 Oct 13; team Oct 14

news.headline: Second life for broken gear: blade recycling at a World Cup, and free body-cord repairs for nonprofit clubs
news.fit: SECONDARY/short (gear tip box; kid-relatable, actionable for parents)
news.summary: FIE says the Takamatsu City World Cup (Japan, Oct 15-18, foil) will host the first broken-blade collection at an official FIE event, feeding the Re-blade 2028 project started by Japanese Olympic champion Kazuyasu Minobe that turns blades into knives, medals and keychains. Separately, USA Fencing profiled Joshua Au's ReCord Initiative, which has repaired and given away 334 body cords to nonprofit clubs and public schools (goal: 500); Absolute Fencing provides collection bins at tournaments.
key_facts: ReCord: 334 cords refurbished; goals 100 → 250 → 500; free labor/parts, recipients pay shipping; recordinitiative.org
Typical body-cord repair cost cited: up to $20
Takamatsu blade collection = first at an official FIE event (blade is foil event; recycling angle is weapon-neutral)
USA Fencing article does not state Joshua Au's age — don't call him a teen unless verified
news.caution: Source does not give Joshua Au's age or home club — don't add either unless verified.
